name: Equifax Inc.
executive_summary: Equifax is a global credit-bureau and workforce-data franchise benefiting from durable demand for verification, fraud and analytics services, with FY2025 operating revenue of $6.07bn (+7% YoY) and strong cash conversion (operating cash flow $1.62bn). The quantitative screen flags the name as a buy on GARP, earnings quality and Piotroski criteria rather than classic deep value — headline P/E of 30.3x and failure on moat/FCF-yield models reflect that tension. H1 2026 revenue accelerated (+12% YoY to $3.35bn), but operating margin compressed to 18.0% and Q2 brought a $100m FCRA litigation accrual; management’s softer near-term outlook triggered a sharp post-earnings sell-off in July 2026. The central debate is whether Workforce Solutions and USIS growth, AI-driven cost savings and aggressive buybacks ($560m in H1 2026) justify elevated leverage and regulatory risk, or whether contract-timing headwinds and royalty-cost inflation cap upside.
investment_thesis:
For a value-oriented investor, EFX is a **quality compounder at a full-ish multiple**, not a statistically cheap stock. The screen passes four distinct families — cheapness (Neff PEGY, Magic Formula), quality (Piotroski F-Score 7/9, Earnings Quality), GARP and risk — with composite score 0.64 versus sector 0.60, data quality 20/20, and a low PEGY of 0.23 that signals growth-adjusted appeal despite P/E 30.3x. Business quality is evident in filings: Workforce Solutions generated 43% of FY2025 revenue and grew 6%; USIS grew 10% on mortgage and diversified markets; consolidated net income rose to $660m (diluted EPS $5.32) from $604m in FY2024.

Cash generation supports the case: FY2025 operating cash flow was $1.62bn against capex of $481m, implying roughly $1.1bn of free cash flow; H1 2026 operating cash flow was $582m. Capital returns are meaningful — FY2025 treasury stock purchases of $928m, a new $3bn repurchase authorisation (April 2025), and the quarterly dividend raised to $0.56 in Q1 2026. Share count fell from 124.0m (Dec 2024) to 117.6m (Jun 2026), aiding per-share metrics.

However, the screen **fails** Graham, Deep Value, FCF Yield, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat and High Dividend Yield — confirming this is not a margin-of-safety deep-value entry. Piotroski misses on leverage declining and current ratio improving, consistent with rising net debt. Conviction on the screen is only 31% (new signal, one week). Filings support a **buy on business quality and GARP**, not on absolute cheapness.
financial_review:
*Primary source: SEC filing body extracts unless noted.*

**Annual results (10-K)**

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | Source |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Operating revenue | $5,265.2m | $5,681.1m | $6,074.5m | FY2025 10-K segment note |
| Net income (Equifax) | $545.3m | $604.1m | $660.3m | FY2025 10-K |
| Diluted EPS | $4.40 | $4.84 | $5.32 | FY2025 10-K |
| Operating cash flow | $1,116.8m | $1,324.5m | $1,615.7m | FY2025 10-K cash flow statement |
| Capex | $601.3m | $511.5m | $481.4m | FY2025 10-K |
| Total debt (gross) | — | $5,037.7m | $5,114.2m | FY2025 10-K |
| Long-term debt, net | — | $4,322.8m | $4,055.3m | FY2025 10-K |
| Cash | — | $169.9m | $180.8m | FY2025 10-K |
| Share repurchases | $0 | $0 | $927.5m | FY2025 10-K |

Revenue CAGR 2023–2025 is approximately 7% annually; net income grew roughly 10% in FY2025. Segment mix is increasingly skewed to Workforce Solutions (Verification Services $2.18bn, +8% YoY in FY2025). Depreciation and amortisation rose to $727m in FY2025, reflecting ongoing cloud/technology investment; restructuring charges of $49.9m were recorded in FY2025 for headcount and contract terminations tied to the cloud transformation.

**Balance sheet and leverage (FY2025 10-K):** Total assets $11.86bn; goodwill $6.75bn. Commercial paper outstanding was $762m at year-end; revolver availability $0.7bn. Revolver covenant requires maximum leverage (consolidated funded debt / EBITDA) of 3.75x; the company **was in compliance** at 31 December 2025. Pension and other post-retirement liabilities were $103m — modest relative to scale. No going-concern language appears in available extracts.

**Interim results (10-Q)**

*Q2 2026 (three months ended 30 June 2026):*
- Operating revenue **$1,700.1m** (+11% YoY; +1% FX)
- Operating income **$314.2m**; operating margin **18.5%** (vs 20.2% in Q2 2025)
- Net income attributable to Equifax **$183.9m**; diluted EPS **$1.54**
- USIS +17%, Workforce Solutions +7%, International +8%

*H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026):*
- Operating revenue **$3,349.0m** (+12% YoY)
- Operating income **$601.9m**; margin **18.0%** (vs 18.4%)
- Net income **$355.4m**; diluted EPS **$2.96** (+14% YoY)
- Operating cash flow **$581.7m** (vs $585.0m H1 2025 — flat)
- Share repurchases **$560m**; dividend **$1.12/share**

*Q3 2025 (derived from nine-month minus six-month figures in filing bodies):*
- Operating revenue approximately **$1,544.9m** (9M 2025 $4,523.9m less H1 $2,979.0m) vs **~$1,441.8m** in Q3 2024 — roughly +7% YoY

**Balance sheet trend at interim (30 Jun 2026 10-Q):** Total debt **$5,485.3m** (commercial paper **$1,397m**, up from $762m at year-end); net debt rose materially. Revolver was upsized to **$2.0bn** in Q2 2026; availability **$0.6bn**. Interest expense H1 2026 **$115.5m** (+9% YoY); average cost of debt 4.3%.

**Margin and cost dynamics:** Filings attribute margin pressure to higher royalty/revenue-share costs, amortisation of capitalised software, and litigation expense (FCRA coding-issue settlement accrual of **$100m** in Q2 2026, net charge **$40m** after a **$60m** insurance receivable). Cost of services rose 17% in H1 2026 vs revenue +12%.

**Gaps:** Eight 8-K filings in the index lack downloadable body extracts; Q3 2026 guidance and any Mexico acquisition terms are not fully verifiable from filing bodies alone — news references a **$750m Mexico credit-bureau deal** and Q3 revenue guidance of **$1.68–1.71bn**, but these figures are **not confirmed in available 10-Q/10-K extracts** and should be treated as unverified from primary filings.
risks_and_flags:
**Regulatory and litigation:** Persistent FCRA exposure. The Q2 2026 10-Q records an agreement in principle to settle nationwide claims from a 2022 coding issue that affected credit scores; **$100m accrued** (net **$40m** P&L impact after insurance). Separately, inquiry-dispute class actions accrued **$30m** in Q4 2025. Filings state Equifax will defend if settlements are not finalised or approved. This reinforces post-2017 breach regulatory sensitivity not captured by quantitative screens.

**Leverage and covenants:** Gross debt rose from $5.1bn (Dec 2025) to $5.5bn (Jun 2026), driven by commercial paper ($1.4bn) and share repurchases. Piotroski’s leverage-decline test failed. Revolver leverage covenant (3.75x EBITDA, extendable to 4.25x for material acquisitions) was met at year-end 2025; **interim covenant compliance is not explicitly stated** in the Q2 2026 extract — a verify-before-trade gap. Termination fees on outsourced IT contracts (Google and others, agreements through 2033) could be material if contracts are exited early.

**Cyclical exposure:** FY2025 10-K and Q2 2026 MD&A note US mortgage originations expected slightly below 2025 levels; ~77% of revenue is US-based. Economic uncertainty, inflation and interest rates may affect credit-inquiry volumes and mortgage-linked revenue.

**Competitive and structural:** Duopoly dynamics (Experian, TransUnion) provide moat in practice, but the screen fails Economic Moat and Buffett Quality — consistent with high intangible asset base (goodwill $6.8bn) and full valuation. Royalty/revenue-share inflation is compressing Workforce Solutions margins (44.9% in Q2 2026 vs 46.4% prior year).

**Governance / capital allocation:** Aggressive buybacks while increasing CP borrowings raises questions about timing versus near-term guidance softness. Redeemable noncontrolling interest in Brazil ($121m) may require future cash outflows. No going-concern issues identified; pension underfunding is limited ($103m liability).

**Pension:** Non-current pension/post-retirement liability $103m (Dec 2025); not a primary red flag.
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is **material and earnings-heavy**, not thin.

**Q2 2026 earnings (21 Jul 2026):** Multiple outlets report results broadly in line but a weak outlook — e.g. “Equifax (NYSE:EFX) Reports Q2 CY2026 In Line With Expectations But Stock Drops 12.1%” (Barchart, 21 Jul 2026); “Why Equifax Stock Is Tumbling Today” (Motley Fool, 21 Jul 2026); “Equifax slides as 2026 outlook disappoints despite solid Q2 growth” (Quiver Quantitative, 21 Jul 2026). Yahoo Finance (“Equifax’s AI Savings, Buybacks and Mexico Deal Could Be A Game Changer”, 22 Jul 2026) cites Q2 revenue **$1,700.1m**, Q3 guidance **$1.68–1.71bn** revenue and **$2.15–2.25** EPS, completion of a **$1.49bn** repurchase programme, and a **$750m** Mexico acquisition — **these guidance/M&A figures are from news, not filing bodies**.

**Analyst reaction (22–24 Jul 2026):** Widespread price-target cuts while ratings largely maintained — e.g. “These Analysts Slash Their Forecasts On Equifax After Q2 Results” (Sahm, 22 Jul 2026); Barclays PT lowered to $200, RBC to $194, Wells Fargo to $212, Needham to $245 (GuruFocus, 23 Jul 2026). Oppenheimer flagged Q3 pressure from contract-signing delays (“Equifax Q3 Outlook Pressured by Contract Signing Delays”, Yahoo Finance, 24 Jul 2026).

**Strategy / capital returns:** Board approved **$3bn** repurchase authorisation (April 2025, per Q2 2026 10-Q MD&A). Dividend raised to **$0.56/quarter** from Q1 2026. Debt issuance noted in “Is Equifax (EFX) A Bargain As New Debt Clouds Its Valuation?” (Yahoo Finance, 22 Jul 2026).

**Other:** Equifax Market Pulse Index on US middle-class pressure (PR Newswire, 8 Jul 2026). Annual meeting 8 May 2025 — directors re-elected, say-on-pay approved, supermajority provisions eliminated (8-K body extract).

**Management changes:** No CEO transition in the news manifest; Mark W. Begor remains board-listed at the 2025 AGM.
research_rationale: Filings confirm a high-quality, cash-generative franchise with accelerating revenue, but rising leverage, litigation accruals, margin compression and a disappointing near-term outlook (news-sourced) temper the quantitative buy signal rather than fully validating deep-value cheapness.
